title: Warranty Claim Document Processing
summary: Pre-check dealer warranty claims before OEM submission: extract job card, VIN, odometer, labour and parts data, test it against policy and flag gaps for the warranty desk.

seo.title: Warranty Claim Document Processing with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that assembles and pre-checks automotive warranty claims: VIN, odometer, labour codes, parts and photos against OEM policy, before submission.

problem.intro: Every warranty repair ends in a claim pack: the repair order, technician notes, labour operation codes, causal part, failed-part photos, odometer and VIN photos and often a diagnostic report. OEMs reject or debit claims for missing photos, mismatched VINs, labour beyond standard time or coverage that had already lapsed, and dealers usually find out only after submission.

pain_points.title: Avoidable rejections
pain_points.detail: Claims bounce for missing odometer photos, unclear failure descriptions or wrong labour codes that could have been caught at the dealer.

pain_points.title: Debits after audit
pain_points.detail: Paid claims that are later audited can be debited back when evidence is thin, hitting dealer margins long after the repair.

pain_points.title: Inconsistent failure narratives
pain_points.detail: Technicians describe the same fault in different words, so complaint, cause and correction rarely line up with the causal part.

pain_points.title: Patterns hidden in volume
pain_points.detail: On the OEM side, repeat repairs on the same VIN, unusual labour times or duplicate claims are hard to spot one claim at a time.

solution.overview: We build a warranty claim assistant that pulls the job card and invoice from your DMS along with photos and diagnostic reports. It extracts VIN, odometer, repair dates, labour operation codes, causal and consequential parts and technician notes, and reads the VIN and odometer photos to confirm they match. Rules configured from the OEM warranty manual check coverage period, mileage, part eligibility, campaign applicability and standard labour times. The technician's notes are structured into complaint, cause and correction without adding facts. Gaps and rule failures go to the warranty manager, who approves every pack before it leaves as a portal-ready claim with an evidence index.
capabilities: Extracts VIN, odometer, repair dates, labour operation codes and parts from job cards and invoices
Reads VIN and odometer photos and checks them against the job card
Checks coverage period, mileage, part eligibility, campaigns and standard labour times from the OEM manual
Structures technician notes into complaint, cause and correction, using only what the notes say
Flags missing photos, duplicate claims and repeat repairs on the same VIN
Prepares a portal-ready claim pack and tracks OEM responses and rejection codes

workflow.title: Collect the claim pack
workflow.detail: Job card, invoice, failed-part photos, VIN and odometer photos and diagnostic reports are pulled from the DMS and upload folders.

workflow.title: Extract and read
workflow.detail: Fields are extracted from documents, and VIN and odometer values are read from photos.

workflow.title: Check policy and consistency
workflow.detail: Rules test coverage, mileage, part eligibility, campaign status and labour times, and cross-check documents against each other.

workflow.title: Warranty manager review
workflow.detail: Claims with gaps go to the warranty manager to fix, justify or hold, and every pack is approved before submission.

workflow.title: Submit to the OEM
workflow.detail: Approved claims are submitted through the OEM warranty portal, by API where available.

workflow.title: Learn from responses
workflow.detail: Approvals, rejections and debit reasons are tracked and used to tune the pre-checks.

inputs: Repair order or job card with technician notes
Tax invoice for parts and labour
Diagnostic tool reports with fault codes
OEM warranty manual, labour time standards and campaign lists
outputs: Portal-ready claim pack with evidence index
Audit trail of checks and edits
human_in_the_loop: The warranty manager reviews every flagged claim and approves each pack before submission. On the OEM side, warranty analysts make every approval and rejection decision; the system prepares and flags.
integrations: OEM warranty portal, by API or controlled browser automation where the OEM permits
guardrails: Policy rules taken from the current OEM manual and version-controlled
Narratives structured only from technician notes, with no facts added
Photo reuse and tamper checks across claims
Nothing submitted without warranty manager approval
Full audit trail for OEM warranty audits
compliance_notes: Customer names and contact details on job cards handled under the DPDP Act 2023.
Keeps the evidence trail dealers need when OEM warranty audits review paid claims.

pilot.scope: One dealer group's warranty claims for one brand, including a backtest on recently rejected claims and live pre-checks on new claims.

Extraction and pre-check pipeline on your claims
Backtest report comparing flags with actual OEM rejection reasons
Roll-out plan for other brands and branches

what_we_measure.how: Backtest of pre-check flags against the rejection and debit reasons the OEM actually gave.
Time per claim at the warranty desk with and without the assistant.
Acceptance of pilot claims at first submission, tracked against the dealer's recent history.
Changes the warranty manager makes to extracted fields and narratives.

faqs.q: Can it submit claims to our OEM's portal?
faqs.a: Where the OEM provides an API we use it. Otherwise the assistant prepares a portal-ready pack and, only where the OEM allows it, a controlled browser automation step enters the claim after approval.
Yes. On the OEM side, the same extraction and rules support warranty analysts reviewing incoming claims, with extra checks for duplicates, repeat repairs and unusual labour across the dealer network.

faqs.q: Does it write the failure description for the technician?
faqs.a: It structures what the technician wrote into complaint, cause and correction and points out missing elements. It does not invent symptoms, causes or tests that are not in the notes.

faqs.q: Our group handles several brands. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. Each brand's warranty manual becomes its own rule set, and the review screen shows which rules applied to each claim.
